title: West Edmeston Tree No More: Its Journey To NYC Is Underway - CNY News
content: Like many, I have driven past this tree off State Route 8 in West Edmeston for years, it's almost like a local landmark or one of those "oh I know where I am" markers. Now all that's left of the 76-foot Norway Spruce are the memories and lots of pictures. This process didn't happen overnight, it's a month's long endeavor with various local state and Rockefeller Center groups coming together to bring a showstopping spectacle to New York City for millions to see. READ MORE: The 2026 Rockefeller Tree Has Been Chosen, From Central New York Shortly before 7am November 5th, cranes were in place ready to lift this year's Rockefeller Tree from the ground and onto a flatbed. Family and friends gathered at the sight surrounded by plenty of media buzz as well. Current owners of the property at 6526 New York 8 we're excited to see the joy that one tree can bring to millions of people around the world. Rebecca Decker told us once she found out the tree's history and the fact this Christmas 2026 marked the 10th anniversary of the death of the person who planted it, she didn't think twice about donating it. Decker remembered the moment someone from the Rockefeller Center first came to her door and asked about the tree. Erik Pauzé, head gardener and head tree scout for Rockefeller Center was that person. Pauzé remembered when he first saw the tree and made sure to write the address down for a potential future tree. As the hour passed by, crews began their finishing touches before the chainsaw came out. There was some laughter and at one point some were spectacle that the tree was going to come down. The chainsaw operator had a difficult time getting the saw to start. But eventually the engine came to life and the cutting started. Within five minutes, the tree was hoisted above its stump. Cheers from the crowd could be heard and I'm sure some happy tears as well. Crews took a once vertical standing tree and carefully laid it horizontal onto the flatbed. From cut to truck, the process took well over an hour. The only thing left was a plot of dirt once shadowed by the Norway Spruce. READ MORE: Santa For Seniors Returns To Bring Christmas Cheer To Seniors In Central New York Department of Transportation officials and members from the Rockefeller Center say the trip won't take long but expect a lot of attention on the way to NYC. Erik Pauzé said they will drive as far as they can today before stopping at a secure location overnight. By Saturday, the once West Edmeston tree will be in New York City for the annual meet the tree day celebration. We were told that 50 thousand lights are set to light up this tree and the official tree lighting ceremony takes place December 2nd at 7pm. title: Social landlords report tenant satisfaction rise in latest TSM results - HQN
content:
English social landlords have reported an increase in the average level of tenant satisfaction, the Regulator of Social Housing (RSH) has revealed. The latest Tenant Satisfaction Measures (TSM) results show an average increase from 72% last year to 74% for 2025/26 for tenants living in low-cost rental accommodation (LCRA). Telephone surveys remain the most widely used collection method and the RSH says overall satisfaction has increased in every collection method, including by telephone where the proportion of tenants reporting they are satisfied overall has increased from 71% to 73%. The new data also shows that landlords have reported improvements in their repairs and maintenance services, with 83% of non-emergency repairs completed on time in 2025/26, compared to 77% in 2023/24. Average (median) satisfaction with the timeliness of repairs has risen from 67% in 2023/24 to 73% in 2025/26, the largest increase across the tenant perception TSMs. Satisfaction with the maintenance of the home has increased from 71% to 74% over the same period. The vast majority of homes owned by large landlords, as at 31 March 2026, had required gas (99.7%), fire (98.9%), asbestos (98.7%), water (98.2%) and lift safety checks (98.0%) completed. These have each increased since TSMs began in 2023/24, with asbestos, water and lift safety having the comparatively largest increases. And 86% of over 319,000 stage one complaints made during 2025/26 were responded to within the Housing Ombudsman’s Complaint Handling Code timescales. This has increased from 73% in the first year of collection (2023/24). The TSMs also provide landlords with valuable information as to how services might be further improved. Around one in six (16%) of LCRA tenants surveyed are dissatisfied with the overall service from their landlord. Overall average (landlord median) satisfaction for low-cost homeownership (LCHO) remains lower (50%) than LCRA, showing that landlords have work to do to improve services and satisfaction for shared owners, the RSH says. Kate Dodsworth, RSH Deputy Chief Executive, said: “The TSM results are based on feedback from almost half a million tenants, providing the most comprehensive view of tenant satisfaction across large social landlords in England. “The increased level of tenant satisfaction reported by landlords underlines the value of landlords listening to tenants, understanding the issues that matter most to them and using those insights to improve services. “Tenant feedback is one of the most important tools landlords have for assessing performance. title: Nickel Asia subsidiaries bag seven awards at inaugural TSM Excellence Awards - Manila Standard
content: Nickel Asia Corporation (NAC) received seven awards through two of its subsidiaries at the Philippines’ first Towards Sustainable Mining (TSM) Excellence Awards.  BuyMaps Rio Tuba Nickel Mining Corporation (RTNMC) and Taganito Mining Corporation (TMC) were among the companies recognized during the inaugural awards ceremony held on October 27 at Conrad Manila in Pasay City. The ceremony was part of the Mining Philippines International Conference and Exhibition, organized by the Chamber of Mines of the Philippines (COMP). BuyMaps “We are here to recognize the companies that don’t just talk about responsible mining as a goal, but live it every day through decisions they make, the systems they build, and the standards they uphold,” said COMP Chairman Michael Toledo in his welcome remarks. TSM awards mining companies that demonstrated excellence in implementing their framework through independently verified assessments. Under the assessment’s five-point scoring scale, ratings of 4.5 to 5.0 qualify for gold tier, while scores of 3.5 to 4.49 qualify for silver tier. The Cross-Cutting Awards recognize broader organizational excellence in implementing responsible mining principles. Companies were evaluated based on four criteria: overall excellence, leadership in sustainable mining, innovation in sustainability systems, and community trust. RTNMC received four gold awards, including Excellence in Community Partnership and Shared Development, Safety Leadership and Zero Harm, and Water Stewardship and Watershed Responsibility. RTNMC was the only gold awardee in the Cross-Cutting category, the top award of the night. Meanwhile, TMC earned a gold award in Excellence in Community Partnership and Shared Development, a silver award in Safety Leadership and Zero Harm, and a silver Cross-Cutting Award. “The awards show us that the Filipino can and will adopt the highest standards that you can find in the leading mining jurisdictions of the world,” NAC Senior Vice President for Sustainability, Risk Management and Corporate Affairs Jose Bayani Baylon said in his acceptance speech for RTNMC’s gold Cross-Cutting Award, delivered on behalf of NAC President and Chief Executive Officer Martin Antonio G. Zamora. He also talked about the importance of communicating the industry’s responsible mining practices and achievements to the public. “Responsible mining exists in the Philippines and that we are one of the best when it comes to adhering to international standards,” he said. The Philippines, through COMP, adopted TSM in 2017, becoming the first country in Asia to implement the internationally recognized mining sustainability framework.
